   CITY OF BEVERLY HILLS
ERLY
  POLICY AND MANAGEMENT

  MEMORANDUM

 TO:  City Council Elections Ad Hoc (Councilmembers Corman and Wells)

 FROM:  Nancy Hunt-Coffey, City Manager

 DATE:  January 22, 2025

 SUBJECT:  Review of portions of the City Council policy manual related to municipal elections

  ATTACHMENT: Page 19 of 2009 version of City Council Policy and Operations
  Manual

Overview
The City Council has been engaged in updating the City Council policy manual which was last
published in 2009. At the September 17, 2024 City Council Study Session, the Council directed
that the Elections Ad Hoc, comprised of Councilmembers Corman and Wells, review the
sections of the policy manual related to elections, such as Mayor and Vice Mayor terms and
when the Council rotations occur.

Background
In 2015, Senate Bill 415 was approved and required cities to hold their elections at the same
time as a statewide election. The City Council changed the election dates to comply with this
new state law. In 2020 the state legislature once again revised its election schedule under SB
970 which impacted the City of Beverly Hills in the following ways:
  • City Council municipal elections now occur in June during non-presidential election
  years and in March in presidential election years.
  • This election pattern is reflected as: March 2020 (presidential election year), June 2022
  (non-presidential election year) and March 2024 (presidential election year) and so on.

It has been the City’s practice to install the Mayor and Vice Mayor annually with an election by
the presiding City Councilmembers. Prior to 2020 during election years, when new City
Councilmembers were elected, they would be installed at the same meeting in March.

However, since 2020 Beverly Hills Municipal Elections have consolidated with statewide
elections, incorporating the new election schedule. The following is the current process in place:

  •  The Mayor and Vice Mayor may still be installed in April of each year, regardless of
  municipal election dates. New Councilmembers elected in March are installed in April as
  well. It should be noted that the LA County Registrar is currently working to formalize
  that all election certifications are to be provided in 30-days, even if the votes are counted
  sooner. This means that in the future the regular installation may need to move to the
  second regular meeting in April, since there may not be 30 days between the March
  election date and the first regular Council meeting date in April.
  •  New Councilmembers elected in June will be installed after the 30-day certification
  process sometime in July.

In short, the Mayor and Vice Mayor are currently installed in April every year.
 New Councilmembers who are elected in June of non-presidential election years are installed in
July. Therefore, in non-presidential election years, the installation of the new MayorNice Mayor
occurs in April and the installation of any new Councilmembers occurs in July, resulting in two
installation ceremonies that year.

As a result of this change in dates, it is feasible that during a non-presidential election year, a
Councilmember could be elected by their fellow Councilmembers to the position of Mayor or
Vice Mayor in April and cease to hold this office in July of the same year because he/she is not
reelected or terms out.

Therefore, the Mayor or Vice Mayor could hold the office for 3 months at which point another
Councilmember would need to be appointed to fill the vacated position in July. Should this
scenario occur, for example, it is not clear if the term as MayorNice Mayor would then be for a
full year (July to July) or for 9 months (July to April).

These changes to the election cycle have led the City Council to express interest in examining
the terms, timing and conditions that need to be met in order to become MayorNice Mayor. At
the September 17th meeting, the City Council tasked the Election Ad Hoc Committee with
working through these issues and returning to the Council with recommendations that can be
incorporated into the City Council policy manual. Some questions to be considered by the Ad
Hoc are:

  •  Should a Mayor or Vice Mayor continue to serve a 1 year term, or when the cycle follows
  the scenario above, should they serve a 3 month term?
  •  If a 3 month term is permitted, then should the subsequent MayorNice Mayor’s term be
  for 9 months (to complete the year) or should the term be for 12 months? Note: If the
  term were for 12 months, over the course of time, the election of MayorNice Mayor
  would shift to different quarters of the year and could lead to other scenarios. For
  example, a Mayor could serve a 6 or 9 month term if they are not re-elected or if they
  term out.
  •  Does the Ad Hoc wish to consider a provision, similar to the Commission Chair rotation,
  where the Mayor must be able to reasonably serve for a year as Mayor.
  •  In either scenario, does a Councilmember have to serve as Vice Mayor before becoming
  Mayor? Would a Councilmember become disqualified from serving as Vice Mayor if they
  are not be able to serve as Mayor due to term limits or due to not being reelected? Note:
  In the past Councilmembers have ascended to the position of Mayor without serving as
  Vice Mayor in the year immediately prior.
  •  Is the Ad Hoc interested in the possibility of moving the municipal elections to
  November, in which case the installation of any new Councilmembers as well as the new
  Mayor and Vice Mayor would occur at the same time every year?

Recommendation
The Ad Hoc is asked to consider the information above and provide recommendations related to
the election of MayorNice Mayor in light of the changes to the election timing. These
recommendations will be brought to the full City Council and, if approved, would be incorporated
in the City Council policy manual.

 Attachment I
 CHAPTER 4  -  Roles and Responsibilities of City Council

MayorNice mayor Selection and Rotation

The mayor and Vice mayor are elected among and by the presiding City Council. Past practice
has provided for the transition of the positions to take place annually during the month of March.

Since 1981, the election of the mayor and Vice mayor is as follows: The Vice mayor position is
rotated each year. The Vice mayor becomes the mayor (except in the cases where the Vice mayor
does not run or is not re-elected).

The position of mayor follows a sequence based on (a) election date and (b) order of finish within
each election. For instance, the third-place vote recipient in the 1998 election would become
mayor before the top vote recipient in the 2000 election. There have been no exceptions made
for seniority or for first time Vice mayors.

Listing Names of councilmembers

The order of presenting City councilmember names follows seniority in the order that
councilmembers rotate into the position of mayor. The first name listed is the mayor, followed by
the Vice mayor. Thereafter, councilmember names are by seniority based on their election as
noted in the preceding section.

Seating on the Dais

Seating on the dais is within the discretion of the mayor. Notwithstanding, historically, seating on
the dais is based on seniority following the rotation established for the position of mayor. Protocol
dictates that the Vice mayor sits to the right of the mayor. To the left of the mayor, sits the
councilmember with the most seniority that would follow the existing Vice mayor in the position of
Vice mayor. To the left of this councilmember, next to the City Attorney, sits the councilmember
with the least seniority. The last remaining seat, beside the Vice mayor and next to the City
Manager, is the councilmember that follows in seniority behind the councilmember sitting to the
left of the mayor.

Role of the mayor

Presiding Officer
The mayor serves as the presiding officer and acts as Chair at all meetings of the City Council.
In this role, the mayor is responsible for maintaining the order and decorum of meetings. The
presiding officer shall also maintain control of communications between councilmembers and
between the City Council and the public. The mayor may participate in all discussions of the
Council in the same manner as any other member. The mayor does not possess any power of
veto. The mayor may make or second, unless otherwise delegated by the City Council, any
motion. The mayor acts as signatory to all documents requiring Council execution. The mayor is
the spokesperson for the Council.

Ceremonial Representative
Responsibility to act as the City Council’s ceremonial representative at public events and
functions has been assigned to the mayor. The mayor is vested with the authority to initiate and
execute proclamations. In the mayor’s absence, the Vice mayor assumes this responsibility.
